newsitem.title: FRANCE: Boutros-Ghali ready to take Francophone post.
newsitem.headline: Boutros-Ghali ready to take Francophone post.

text.p: Boutros Boutros-Ghali, ousted as U.N. secretary-general by the United States last year, has said he is ready to accept the position of secretary-general of the community of French-speaking nations.

Boutros-Ghali, 72, a former Egyptian deputy prime minister who served at the United Nations for five years, indicated on a visit to Poitiers in western France that he was available to take the post, to be created in November.
"I am at the disposal of the Francophone heads of state and government if they decide to call on me," the newspaper Le Monde on Friday quoted him as saying.
He said his aim was "to transform the emotional reality of a Francophone community into a political project...an important instrument to help democratise international relations".

"Along with groupings using Spanish, Portuguese and Arabic, it is a guarantee of diversity in the face of the single cultural model which a minority is tempted to impose and which would be the equivalent of a global one-party state," Boutros-Ghali said.

France has sought to build the 49-nation "Francophonie", created to promote the use of the French language and culture, into an international body akin to the Commonwealth that links Britain and most of its former colonies.

Secretary of State for Francophonie Margie Sudre said on Thursday it was well known France favoured Boutros-Ghali for the post of secretary-general, to be established at the next Francophone summit in Hanoi, Vietnam, on November 14-16.
The veteran diplomat has been living mainly in Paris since Ghana's Kofi Annan succeeded him in New York, friends said.

The United States vetoed his reappointment for a second term, saying a new face was needed to reform the U.N. bureaucracy more thoroughly. Some U.S. officials privately accused Boutros-Ghali of being too close to French positions.
